Ours is untouched base, so this is a clean fast-forward. Real plunge-pool basin (-3.15, smoothstep 5.4..8.2 around z+15.2) in both terrainHeightFn and clearing mesh (they match — no floating-terrain bug); bridge-stone tops become walkable ground once risen; 7 bigger stones (was 5); cliff widened 44->60 with colliders to +-30 (closes a walk-around); game.waterfallBarrier collider physically bars the fall pre-bargain (bridgeBarrier is an alias, line 591 — the director's two names are the SAME object, not a bug); game.caveZone = addZone(...) with enabled = flags.has('waterfallTaken'); caveHatch double-gated on waterfallTaken; rope onArrive adds game.checkpoint('forest') (far-side pose checkpoint); forest seal update pools its Matrix4/Vector3/Quaternion (was allocating per frame). Bug hunt: nothing here explains floating objects or stair see-through; carefully checked.

Three small changes: addZone returns the zone object with enabled:true; zoneAt skips enabled===false; surfaceAt iterates LAST-match-wins. The surfaceAt flip is a genuine bug fix for OUR authoring order — today first-match makes the kitchen flags sound like wood (house wood zone registered before kitchen stone, house.js:569-570), the cave mouth sound like clearing dirt, and the finale bedroom sound like cave stone; last-match fixes all three. Verified every addSurface call site in both trees — no zone relies on first-match. Risk is only prospective: future surface zones must be authored as later-overrides. Does not touch stairs, colliders, or _buildStairs (stairs are solid full-height boxes — the see-through Alex saw is not geometric).

variantCShim: Their src/skull-variant-c.js is a 41-line CALIBRATION SHIM, not a sculpt. It imports buildSkullMesh from skull-variant-a.js, builds variant A's full anatomy/growth rig, then wraps parts.root in a new Group named 'fetchShippingSkull' (userData.variant='c', source='anatomical-a', triangleCount/Budget copied through) and applies three tunes: anatomy root scaled (1.13, 0.97, 1.04) + y -0.002 (broader cranium for the 71-degree viewmodel), jaw hinge closed (parts.jaw.position.y += 0.005, parts.jawMount.position.y += 0.003 — kills the dangling-jaw read without reducing chatter range), and both eye globes scaled 0.8 (less comic-lens at viewmodel scale). It returns {...parts, root} preserving the exact part contract. Their skull.js then makes this the DEFAULT: the variant ternary is `a -> A, b -> B, else -> C`, so NO ?skull param ships their calibrated-A, and the variant-D import is deleted (their tree has no skull-variant-d.js). THE COLLISION: our repo's skull-variant-c.js (21KB) and skull-variant-d.js (29KB) are the round-3 sculpt-off winners mounted at ?skull=c and ?skull=d (commit 83054fe), with the original courier sculpt as the no-param default and Alex judging in-game — same filename, totally different content and intent. A naive file copy would (a) delete sculpt candidate C, and (b) silently change the shipping skull identity, which may not happen without Alex's judgment. CLEAN RECONCILIATION: keep our skull-variant-c.js/d.js and our VARIANTS={a,b,c,d} switch with courier default untouched; port their 41 lines to a NEW file (suggest src/skull-variant-a2.js, 'the calibrated anatomist') exporting the same buildSkullMesh contract, and add `a2: buildVariantA2` to the VARIANTS map so it competes at ?skull=a2 next to a/b/c/d. Their in-hand calibration observations (jaw gap, eye scale at viewmodel FOV) are genuinely useful signal for whichever sculpt wins. After Alex crowns a winner, promote it to default and delete the losers — exactly per the comment already in our _buildMesh. Patch their regression check 'default query ships anatomical variant C' to assert OUR default until then.

summary: Codex's fork branches from our playtest-2 state (2dc1a96) and never saw our furnish audit or skull round 3. Their genuinely good work is systems + spectacle: atmosphere.js (one-ticker, instanced night sky/forest/clearing/cave dress), the rebuilt finale bedroom, the waterfall basin/barrier set piece with persistent post-bargain state, scoped director timers, forward-only acts, pose-restoring checkpoints, structural enemy LOS, and a real bug fix we ship today (Standing Kind V.c scratch-vector alias in our enemies.js:130). Their enemies.js keeps our door-node steering and Resident-opens-doors verbatim — no conflict with playtest 2. All three bugs Alex saw in their build are explained and none import with a correct merge: floating/misplaced objects = our missing audit re-seats (their house.js is base + one key-material hunk); the un-findable basement key and most plausibly the stair see-through = their skull light dimmed to 1.2 in hand (ours is a constant-42 lantern; keep ours or retune well above theirs). Feel core survives untouched: FEEL_PROFILE identical, throw grammar preserved (their clearKeys fix actually defends it on focus loss), player tuning unchanged (they only add a movementLocked flag), our fixed-step loop intact. Three decisions are reserved for Alex: skull default (their skull-variant-c.js is a 41-line variant-A calibration shim colliding by filename with our sculpt-off winner — remount as ?skull=a2, no default change ships), fearHome graveyard short-throws (they deleted it for a cosmetic tremble — keep ours, add their tremble), and crosshair/copy/death-beat presentation. Their tests are worth adopting wholesale (regressions suite, GPU render gate, honest perf labeling, real resident assertion) with exactly two checks patched to our decisions; merge the dependency cluster in one commit and every gate stays green.
